newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: SKorea won ends lower despite central bank actions.
newsitem.headline: SKorea won ends lower despite central bank actions.

text.p: The won slid to a lower close on Thursday despite the central bank's offer to sell dollars in forward trading, traders said.
The central bank's actions, while not stopping the local currency's fall, would help put a floor to the won's decline, they added.
The won ended at 869.20, against an opening high of 868.30. It touched a low of 869.50.
"The central bank wants to keep the 870 level, judging by its offers on the forward markets," said a western bank dealer.
In early afternoon trading, the central bank offered to sell $30 million each at the 883 won level in three-month forward trading and the 897 won level in six-month forward trading.
The central bank has refused to comment on intervention on the interbank market.
Traders said the won was expected to fluctuate widely early next week.

"There are import settlements worth about $500 million coming in, while about $700 million will be sold by off-shore funds," said a European bank dealer. "So the market is nervous about the direction."
The western dealer said he saw the won moving in a 868-870 range on Friday, while the European trader forecast a 869-878 range.
The base midrate was seen pegged at 869.00, compared to Thursday's 867.50.
